input.summary: Meridian's 257 tracked metrics reveal 7 use cases blocked by foundational data and governance gaps before any outcome value can be claimed.
covers: Governed data foundation for AI / LLM automation

story.meaning: All seven CEO-priority use cases are in planning stage — no outcome metric can be claimed until foundational data, identity, governance, and platform evidence gates are closed.
story.observed: 31 of 257 metrics are active; 226 remain candidate-grade. Across all use cases, every metric boundary is flagged baseline_required_before_value_claim, with 24 distinct structural gaps evidenced.
story.matters: Without closing lakehouse, governance, and contract digitization gates, Meridian cannot quantify cost transparency, payment leakage, or quality performance — exposing CFO and CEO commitments to unsubstantiated projections.
story.supports: Prioritize the five evidence gates — medallion architecture, identity spine, data governance operating model, provider contract digitization, and transcript governance — before any board-level outcome metric is published.

findings: Measure logic for provider quality is fragmented across Tableau, Power BI, and Epic Caboodle — no single certified source exists, making HEDIS/STAR reporting ungoverned and dispute-prone.
Payment integrity relies on SAS estate models with no governed lineage or provider entity resolution, meaning leakage magnitude cannot be quantified or defended to the CFO.
Call center optimization is blocked by four concurrent gaps — transcript governance, real-time CRM integration, intent taxonomy, and member identity linkage — none of which are proven.
All seven use cases share a common upstream blocker: no formal data governance operating model and no certified semantic layer, making every downstream metric unauditable.

gaps.handoff: Data Engineering and CDAO office to certify architecture and load identity spine before metric activation

gaps.missing: No formal data governance operating model or certified semantic layer
gaps.blocks: All seven use cases — every metric is unauditable and ungoverned

gaps.handoff: CDAO and Data Governance lead to stand up operating model; gate all metric publishing behind certification

gaps.blocks: Cost transparency and provider quality metrics — margin and attribution calculations cannot be trusted

gaps.handoff: Network Contracting and Finance to digitize and certify contract terms; CFO sign-off required before cost metrics are published

evidence.name: Metrics & Outcomes Dataset — Active Cohort
evidence.facts: 31 metrics are active; 226 are candidate-grade. Confidence split: 187 high, 70 medium. All active metrics carry metric_boundary = baseline_required_before_value_claim.
evidence.fields: use_case, risk_or_gap, affected_systems, metric_boundary, confidence, active_candidate_status, evidence_id
evidence.supports: Confirms no use case has cleared its evidence gate; all outcome metrics are pre-baseline.
evidence.missing: Baseline values, target thresholds, metric owners, and measurement cadence are not yet loaded for any use case.

evidence.name: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse Evidence Bundle
evidence.facts: Medallion architecture, patient/member identity spine, claims/pharmacy harmonization, and AWS/Databricks foundation are all unproven. All four gaps are high or medium confidence.
evidence.supports: Establishes that the foundational lakehouse platform is not ready to support any clinical or cost outcome metric.
evidence.missing: Architecture certification evidence, identity spine load confirmation, and harmonization test results.

evidence.name: Governed Data Foundation for AI / LLM Evidence Bundle
evidence.facts: No formal governance operating model, no certified semantic layer, no AI audit trail, and no data quality rules are evidenced. Three of four gaps are high confidence.
evidence.supports: Confirms that AI/LLM automation metrics cannot be published or defended without governance and lineage controls.
evidence.missing: Governance charter, semantic layer certification, AI audit trail design, and data quality rule inventory.

evidence.name: Provider Quality & Cost Transparency Evidence Bundle
evidence.facts: Measure logic is fragmented across Tableau and Power BI. Attribution ownership is unproven. Provider contract terms are not digitized. Claims and GL calendar alignment is unproven.
evidence.supports: Establishes that provider quality scores and cost margin metrics cannot be trusted or published to the board.
evidence.missing: Single certified measure source, attribution model sign-off, digitized contract repository, and GL reconciliation evidence.

evidence.name: Call Center & Payment Integrity Evidence Bundle
evidence.facts: Transcript governance, real-time integration, intent taxonomy, and member identity linkage are all unproven for call center. SAS model lineage, provider entity resolution, investigation workflow, and recovery tracking are absent for payment integrity.
evidence.supports: Confirms that AHT/FCR baselines and leakage quantification are both pre-evidence and cannot be reported.
evidence.missing: Transcript governance policy, CRM integration proof, intent taxonomy certification, SAS lineage documentation, and recovery workflow instrumentation.

evidence.name: AI Benefits Realization Ledger
evidence.facts: Benefits ledger is loaded but all entries are pre-baseline. No realized value is evidenced. Ledger confirms FY26 AI spend governance is active but outcome tracking is not yet instrumented.
evidence.supports: Confirms that the organization has intent to track AI benefits but no measurement infrastructure is in place.
evidence.missing: Baseline measurements, adoption tracking, workflow instrumentation, and finance sign-off on benefit methodology.
